 Roomerang is the first game to be announced for The Jackbox Party Pack 9 , having been announced on February 18, 2022. The game of responding to prompts, role-playing, and whatever level of competition you bring to the table. Players in a reality TV show world are encouraged to answer prompts through their game personas, to gain status and avoid elimination.

 4 Gallery

 6 Promotional Art 

 7 Trivia 

 Gameplay [ ] 

 Players start out with 5 points and will answer the prompts given to them. They are also given a character description (Ex: Likes Smoothies) Throughout each round, the other players (and audience) will vote on which answers they liked best; each player gets a point if their answer is voted.

 The players then vote on who to eliminate and explain why (Ex: Tulips taste weird in smoothies), and the player with the most votes is eliminated. That player gets a few seconds to type in or say some parting words before the door slams on them. However, this player gets Roomeranged back in with a vowel letter swapped in their name, a clothing item, and a new character description (Ex: BROOKE gets changed to BReOKE with the description "Has Never Worn Shoes"). The next round continues with the newly-swapped player.

 This goes on for five rounds. The first round is an introduction round, where each player answers a question about themselves. The second round is a connections round, where each player is paired up with another and must answer a question that relates to both. The third round is a quickie round, which is done anonymously. The fourth round is a firestarter round, where each player must pick another player and blame them for something. During the final round, the host will ask the group to vote for the player they think should win and the player they think shouldn't win! Players give their reasons, and they're all asked what the best conclusion for the round would be. After that, the points are tallied up and the winner is chosen! That person gets to make a victory speech before they're shown the door and the game ends.

 Trivia [ ] 

 Jackbox Games showed real-time development progress every month in their " Inside the Box " series, providing Twitch audiences with a behind-the-scenes look at the process they goes through when creating its party packages. A total of 8 "Inside the Box" episodes were held, talking about the gameplay of the game.

 The fonts used are Times New Roman, Futura PT Bold, Futura PT Extra Bold & Foundation Sans Roman.

 There are a few used tracks that are not available in the soundtrack.

 In the documentary " Jackbox Games, From Pitch to Party Pack " by Flyover Culture, it's possible to catch glimpses of early character designs for Roomerang, featuring some of the players' beta designs and early concepts for host themselves, as well as concept sketches of the game's early layouts.

 Roomerang is a roleplay party video game and one of five games featured in The Jackbox Party Pack 9 .

 In this game, described as "reality TV-inspired", players assume the role of a reality TV star whose goal is to come out on top, by answering prompts and avoiding elimination.

 Gameplay

 After joining the lobby through the Jackbox.TV controller, the game asks the player to confirm their name, as well as provide brief details about their character. The player could choose from one of three different roles, or type in a custom role.

 Afterwards, they then get to choose one of twelve "roomie" avatars, each with a different monochromatic color. After selecting the avatar, the player's name and avatar they selected appear in the lobby screen, accompanied by their matching voice sound.

 Once the required amount of players are in, the game can begin. The players are introduced to the game's host Rue Meringue (voiced by Dezi Bing ), who guides the players on how to play the game, before she introduces the roomies and their role.

 Each player begins with 5 points in their private bank—no one will know anyone else’s score (except their own on their controller screen) until after the final round.

 The game consists of five rounds. The first four rounds are presented as follows:

 Introductions - Players are given a generic prompt that involves introducing themselves.

 Connections - Players are given a prompt which involves connecting with another player that is randomly selected. The player mentioned in a winning answer receives points, and sometimes can get safety from elimination.

 Quickie - Players are given a generic prompt, except all players' identities are not revealed until after the voting round.

 Firestarter - Players are given a prompt which involves blaming another player and why. It plays similar to Connections, only the player gets to pick another player.

 In each of the first four rounds, players are presented with a challenge where they answer a prompt, preferably in character. (If Audience is turned on, non-players can answer a separate poll.) 

 After all answers are submitted, the responses are revealed one-by-one, before players (and the audience) vote on which is the best.

 After everyone casts their vote (or time runs out), the votes are counted, with each vote representing one point. The player with the most votes wins the challenge, and receives a special advantage —advantages can consist of:

 Safety

 Safety plus giving another chosen player safety

 Safety plus audience gets to choose who to eliminate (Only available when Audience mode is turned on.) 

 Safety plus player mentioned gets safety (Only available in Rounds 2 and 4.) 

 Swapping points with another player (Only available in Rounds 3 and 4.) 

 Winner chooses who to eliminate (Their vote is also doubled.) 

 Winner chooses who to eliminate that voted for the winning answer (Their vote is also doubled.) 

 Winner's vote counts as two

 Winner can cancel another player's vote

 Next, comes the elimination : Players (except the winner with safety) will have to vote on who should leave the Roomerang house, and why. After the votes are casted, Rue Meringue reveals who got eliminated in an animated sequence where she pulls out a card from an envelope, before coming up close to the screen and showing the eliminated player name on the card. (The animation gets slightly faster per round.) 

 The "eliminated" player is then given a chance to send a goodbye message before the doors are shut on them—however they quickly come back with an accessory (such as a hat, glasses, or mustache), as well as  a new name and role. (If family-friendly mode is turned off, the first vowel in the player's name is always changed. If it's turned on, an affix is added to their existing name instead.) 

 Throughout the game, players can access an inbox on the bottom-left corner of their controller, so they can see who tried to eliminate them previously or who won the challenge, giving them suggestions on who to eliminate next.

 After the first four rounds are finished, players move onto the Finale Round , where players are given one final prompt to answer, usually involving a lesson, moral, or learning experience.

 After all responses are submitted, players then vote on who they think should win the game—point values are doubled per vote. Afterwards, players then vote and who should NOT win the game, with a point taken away from a player that receives a vote.

 After the final round has concluded, the final scores are shown in ascending order, until the top 2 players are shown side-by-side. The player with the most points at the end of the game wins, and has an opportunity to put in a victory speech, before the door is inevitably closed on them.

 If there is a tie with 2 or more players, there is an algorithm that goes like this (in order):

 The player with the most "who should win" votes is the winner.

 If above still results in a tie, the player with the least "who shouldn't win" votes is the winner.

 If above still results in a tie, the player picked by the audience to win is the winner.

 If above still results in a tie, then a random player is chosen as the winner.

 During the end credits, the VIP can replay a game with the same players, continuing the season where they left off with the same identities—however the scores are reset. (Starting with Party Pack 9's November update, an option was added to keep scores entering into another game.)
